q: Patient with extreme photosensitivity, skin mottling and basal cell tumors; the DNA-repair process that is broken here is:
ex: In xeroderma pigmentosum NER is bstant — the culprit of ultraviolet-induced 6-4 photoproducts accum.

q: Which PCR strategy is best to detect several different pathogens simultaneously from one cerebrospinal-fluid sample in suspected meningitic syndrome?
ex: Multiplex PCR runs multiple primer pairs per tube with distinct-size amplicons — is a 'one tube, many bugs' method.

q: In an isolated-perfused mito experiment, a single-established inhibitor that blocks NADH dehydrogenase of electron transport chain is:
ex: Rotenone (complex I) and amytal; antimycin III, cyanide/CO IV, olighene V.

q: A 28-year-old with 2 months amenorrhea shows linea nigra, Montgomery tubercles and a bluish discoloration of the vagina. How are such signs classified?
ex: Chadwick sign, Hegar sign, uterine enlargement are probable; fetal heartbeat/USG are positive signs.

q: A multipara with preceding obstructed labour now has continuous urine dribbling per vagina. Where does the resulting obstetric vesicovaginal fistula most commonly lie?
o: Supratrigonal/trigonal area of the anterior vaginal wall
ex: Prolonged labour causes the anterior vaginal supratrigonal fistula from pressure of the presenting part.

q: A 17-year-old with primary amenorrhea has no breast or pubic hair growth, absent uterus on ultrasound, and bilateral inguinal swellings. What is the diagnosis?
ex: 46,XY AIS: scanty pubic hair despite testes in inguinal region, uterus absent, no pubertal milestones.

q: A 16-year-old with 5 months cyclcyl lower pain, no menarche, and a bluish bulging membrane at the introitus most likely has:
ex: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, suprapubic tightness, bulging bluish hymen at the introitus.

q: A 46-year-old nullipara has irregular heavy cycles for a year and endometrial thickness 18 mm on transvaginal scan. What is the next best step?
ex: Thickened endometrium in perimenopause clinics a transvagabound, cytologic/hysteroscopic endometrial biopsy.

q: A 55-year-old postmenopausal lady notes blood-stained vaginal discharge; casual BP is 170/100 mmHg. What is the best next step?
o: Immediate pelvic examination, transvaginal ultrasound and Pap smear
Start antihypertensives and review in a week
Cardiology referral before any pelvic exam
ex: Any postmenopausal bleeding mandates gynaecological evaluation to rule out endometrial/cervical cancer.

q: During IVF cycle stimulation with hMG, a 30-year-old develops sudden abdominal distention, pain, nausea and deepening breathlessness. The ovaries are enlarged with ascites on USG. What is the diagnosis?
ex: OHSS from FSH-driven multiple folliculogenesis + hCG trigger; severe form with ascites and hypovolemia.

q: During hysteroscopic myomectomy, a fluid deficit of 2000 mL is measured. What immediate complication is expected?
o: TURP syndrome- hyponatremia with cerebral edema
ex: Irrigation fluid excess causes dilutional hyponatremia cerebral edema; stop and diuretic/manage sodium.

q: A multipara delivered at home by a trained dai now shows a uterine prolapse. Which stretch of tissue is predominantly responsible for loss of support?
ex: Level I/II support by cardinal-uterosacral complex holds the uterus; injury leads to prolapse.

q: A first-trimester pregnant woman had toxoplasmosis in the past and is IgG positive, IgM negative. What is the correct advice?
o: No risk to this fetus; same immunity as prior infection, no active infection
ex: IgG+ IgM- means past protected infection; she cannot re-acquire toxoplasmosis.

q: In gestational diabetes of the mother, which macromolecule does NOT cross the placenta to the fetus?
ex: Fetal insulin is endogenous; only glucose crosses, driving fetal hyperinsulinemia and macrosomia.

q: During active labor the cervicograph crosses the action line of the partograph. What is the interpretation?
o: Labor is not progressing and needs active review/intervention
ex: Crossing the action/alert lines indicates further labor dysfunction; decide augmentation or cesarean.

q: A patient with cervical carcinoma presents with unilateral hydronephrosis due to parametrial disease extending to the pelvic wall. What FIGO stage is this?
ex: Extension to the lateral pelvic wall and/or hydronephrosis due to ureteric obstruction = stage IIIB.

q: A 68-year-old woman has a 3 cm ulcerative invasive vulvar cancer with two palpable mobile 1 cm left inguinal nodes. What is the FIGO stage?
ex: Tumor with 2 inguinal lymph nodes each ≥1 cm metastasis is vulvar stage IIIB.

q: A young lady has foul smelling, frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge and a strawberry patterned itchy cervix. The likely organism is:
ex: Strawberry cervix with frothy discharge = Trichomoids; treated with metronidazole.

q: Medical Termination of Pregnancy at 27 weeks for a major fetal anomaly is permitted in India only when:
o: A medical board approves due to fetal abnormality
One eligible woman can decide in private
ex: MTP Amendment 2021: for anomalies beyond 24 weeks, a constituted medical board must approve.

q: Which of the following is acceptable/appropriate and NOT an absolute contraindication for induction of labor?
ex: Post-dates is a valid indication; transverse lie, scar and grade 4 previa contraindicate induction.

q: A woman at 8 weeks gestation attends a dating scan. Which sonographic parameter is most accurate for pregnancy dating now?
ex: CRL (7-13 wk) is the best estimate; after 13 wks, BPD/head and femur take over.

q: A 36-year-old with 6 months of secondary amenorrhea has hormonal FSH 36, LH 56 and AMH 0.06 ng/mL. What is the likely diagnosis?
ex: Serum FSH raised, AMH very low and young — primary ovarian insufficiency leading to early menopause.

q: Which of these decreases during P1an expected throughout normal pregnancy?
ex: Plasma volume expands ~50% exceeding RBC, diluting hemoglobin in physiological fall.

q: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy is most commonly observed during which gestational period?
ex: AFLF typically develops in the late third (third) trimester with hypoglycemia and liver failure.

q: A DM patient undergoing cesarean began magnesium sulfate. She now becomes drowsy with respiratory rate 10/min, absent knee jerks and oliguria despite a blood glucose of 240 mg/dL. The cause is:
ex: Mg toxicity: loss of deep reflexes, bradyspnea, oliguria; gives calcium gluconate.

q: A 26-week pregnancy shows a fundal height corresponding to 24 weeks, with reduced amniotic fluid on scan. Among the causes is: which one is the most important?
ex: Oligohydramnios follows critical fetal anuria with the classical bilateral renal agenesis usually.

q: A 35-year-old woman with metastatic choriocarcinoma in lung/spleen/kidney, previous mole 6 months back, source hCG 10,000 IU/L & failed MTX. Best next is:
ex: High-risk GTN foundation: EMA-CO (etoposide, MTX, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide, vincristine).

q: Atonic postpartum hemorrhage does not respond to uterine massage and parenteral oxytocin. Which of the following is the next best step to perform in the labour room?
ex: As a first-line surgical step: intrauterine balloon tamponade; then compression sutures/ligation.

q: A G2P1L1 with previous lower segment cesarean in trial of labor has non- pacifying suprapubic pain, fetal bradycardia, maternal tachycardia and cervix 8 cm dilated. Next step is:
ex: Suspect uterine scar rupture; stop oxytocics and do upstream emergency LSCS.

q: During episiotomy repair, what is the correct sequence of tissue layers repaired?
o: Vaginal mucosa → perineal muscles → fascia → skin
ex: Start at the vaginal apex to recreate the anatomy: mucosa, muscles, then skin.

q: While delivering a breech fetus the scapula becomes visible and the arms lie extended. Which maneuver should free the extended arms?
ex: Lovset maneuver rotates the fetal body so extended arms come down to the navel.

q: Medical MTP at 9 weeks in a 25-year-old is best done with which combination?
ex: First-trimester medical MTP: mifepristone 200 mg then misoprostol 48 h later.

q: A woman with a past twin delivery who is pregnant again has an obstetric score written as:
ex: Gravida counts gestation, parity counts deliveries — previous twin birth counts as P1 with two living.

q: Which previous-year trend item is correctly matched with its FIGO staging?
o: Postoperative disease extension in ovarian cancer documented within 3 mo of treatment
Data based on surgery in ovarian
Hydronephrosis in cervical PID auto IIIB
ex: Cervical cancer with hydronephrosis from pelvic wall extension = IIIB; ovarian cancer is surgical stage.

q: A 3-week-old neonate has fever, lethargy and seizures. Blood culture on sheep blood agar, streaked perpendicular to a Staphylococcus aureus line, shows an arrowhead zone of enhanced hemolysis. Which organism is confirmed by this positive CAMP test?
ex: CAMP factor produced by Group B Streptococcus (S. agalactiae) enlarges the hemolytic zone of S. aureus beta-hemolysin, giving an arrowhead pattern.

q: An HIV-positive man has a painless, beefy-red genital ulcer that bleeds on touch, without inguinal lymphadenopathy. Giemsa-stained smear shows intracytoplasmic organisms with a safety-pin appearance. The causative agent is:
ex: Donovan bodies (bipolar safety-pin bacilli in macrophages) are pathognomonic of granuloma inguinale caused by Klebsiella granulomatis.

q: An asymptomatic employee is HBsAg and HBeAg positive on screening, with mildly raised ALT. What does HBeAg positivity signify in this patient?
o: High viral infectivity and active replication
Immune clearance phase with low viremia
ex: HBeAg correlates with active HBV replication and high infectivity; its loss with anti-HBe seroconversion marks declining infectivity.

q: A farmer from eastern India has chronic cough, weight loss and mediastinal lymphadenopathy with calcified hilar nodes on chest X-ray. Culture grows a mould at 25°C but yeast forms at 37°C. The most likely fungus is:
ex: Histoplasma capsulatum is a dimorphic fungus: mycelial at 25°C, intracellular yeast at 37°C; chronic infection mimics TB with hilar calcification.

q: A patient with subacute meningitis has clear CSF with lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, high protein and a cobweb coagulum on standing. The most likely etiological agent is:
ex: Tubercular meningitis classically yields clear CSF, lymphocytosis, hypoglycorrhachia and a fibrin web (coagulum) on standing.

q: A young adult has dry cough and fever, but chest X-ray shows diffuse infiltrates far more extensive than the clinical state. Cold agglutinins are positive. The likely pathogen is:
ex: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes atypical pneumonia with antibody-mediated cold agglutinins and X-ray-clinical dissociation.

q: A neonate with an umbilical stump infection develops generalized muscle rigidity and risus sardonicus. The mechanism of the responsible toxin is:
o: Blocks release of inhibitory neurotransmitters GABA and glycine
Inhibits protein synthesis by ADP-ribosylation of EF-2
ex: Tetanospasmin binds gangliosides and blocks GABA/glycine release at inhibitory synapses, producing spastic paralysis.

q: A patient from a rural area has fever, headache, myalgia and an eschar at a tick bite site. Weil-Felix test shows agglutination of OX-K antigen. The infecting agent is:
ex: Scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi) gives OX-K agglutinins in the Weil-Felix test; OX-19 positivity suggests typhus group rickettsiae.

q: A patient develops bloody diarrhea after eating raw oysters. The stool isolate is a halophilic curved gram-negative rod giving a positive Kanagawa phenomenon. The organism is:
ex: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is halophilic, sea-food associated, and its beta-hemolysis on Wagatsuma agar (Kanagawa phenomenon) marks enteropathogenic strains.

q: A patient with chronic pneumonia has skin and bone lesions. Microscopy of pus shows large, thick-walled yeast cells with broad-based budding. The fungus is:
ex: Blastomyces dermatitidis is identified by broad-based budding yeasts, unlike the narrow-necked budding of Cryptococcus.

q: A young woman has dysuria and frequency. Urine culture grows a coagulase-negative, novobiocin-resistant staphylococcus (>10^5 CFU/mL). The likely organism is:
ex: S. saprophyticus, the second commonest cause of uncomplicated UTI in young women, is novobiocin-resistant and coagulase-negative.

q: A 6-year-old with fever and a slapped-cheek rash develops sudden pallor and severe reticulocytopenia. The virus most likely causing this aplastic crisis is:
ex: Parvovirus B19 infects erythroid precursors; in chronic hemolytic states it causes transient aplastic crisis with reticulocytopenia.

q: A man with chronic leg swelling following an insect bite develops warty, cauliflower-like skin lesions. Biopsy shows copper-penny bodies (sclerotic cells). The diagnosis is:
ex: Chromoblastomycosis follows traumatic implantation; muriform sclerotic bodies (copper-penny/medlar cells) are seen in tissue.

q: A poorly controlled diabetic recovering from COVID-19 develops facial pain, nasal discharge and black eschar. Biopsy shows broad, nonseptate hyphae branching at right angles. The causative agent is:
ex: Mucormycosis shows wide, ribbon-like aseptate hyphae with right-angle branching, typically in ketoacidotic or immunocompromised hosts.

q: A woman with extensive anogenital warts is at high risk of cervical carcinoma. The HPV types most often implicated in malignant transformation are:
ex: High-risk HPV 16/18 (E6/E7 oncoproteins) drive cervical and anogenital cancers; 6/11 cause benign genital warts.

q: An HIV patient with CD4 count below 100 has chronic diarrhea, fever and malabsorption. Stool smear shows acid-fast organisms. The likely agent is:
ex: Mycobacterium avium complex causes disseminated disease with diarrhea in advanced AIDS; MAC is acid-fast and stains with modified ZN.

q: A patient with fever, retro-orbital pain and a petechial rash has thrombocytopenia. Early in illness, which test confirms dengue infection most rapidly?
ex: NS1 antigen is detectable from day 1 of dengue fever, before IgM antibodies appear (day 5 onward).

q: Which statement about Trichomonas vaginalis infection is correct?
o: Cysts are the infective form passed between partners
It cannot be cultured on artificial media
Wet mount shows trophozoites with jerky, twitching motility
It is exclusively transmitted by fomites
ex: Trichomonas vaginalis has only a trophozoite stage, which shows characteristic jerky motility on a wet mount; it is sexually transmitted.

q: A child with fever and rash has urine cytology showing cells with owl-eye intranuclear inclusions. The likely virus is:
ex: CMV produces large cells with owl-eye intranuclear inclusions in urine, CSF and tissue; urine is the preferred specimen in congenital infection.

q: Chronic infection with Clonorchis sinensis predisposes to which malignancy?
ex: Liver flukes (Clonorchis, Opisthorchis) and Schistosoma haematobium are classic parasite-cancer associations (cholangiocarcinoma, bladder cancer).

q: A sewage worker has fever, abdominal pain, jaundice, conjunctival suffusion and hematuria. The serological test of choice to confirm his infection is:
ex: Microscopic agglutination test (MAT) is the reference serological test for leptospirosis, the classic occupational waterborne zoonosis.

q: A woman with curdy white vaginal discharge has budding yeast with pseudohyphae on smear. Which medium best differentiates the Candida species?
ex: CHROMagar differentiates Candida species by colony color; bird seed agar is specific for Cryptococcus neoformans.

q: A soldier has fever, severe myalgia and a maculopapular rash that spares the palms and soles; body lice are found on examination. The most likely agent is:
ex: Epidemic louse-borne typhus (R. prowazekii) classically spares the palms and soles, unlike rickettsial spotted fevers.

q: An HIV patient has fever, cough and breathlessness. Culture yields a fungus that is a mold at 25°C but a yeast at 37°C. Which agent is most likely?
ex: Talaromyces marneffei, a dimorphic fungus of Southeast Asia, is a mold at 25°C and a fission yeast at 37°C in AIDS patients.

q: A newborn of an HIV-positive mother develops diarrhea. Which test establishes the infant's HIV status most reliably?
o: HIV antibody ELISA in the neonate
Stool microscopy for ova and cysts
ex: Maternal IgG crosses the placenta, so serology is unhelpful; HIV DNA/RNA PCR in the first weeks is diagnostic in infants.

q: A 28-year-old woman is HBsAg positive and IgM anti-HBc positive, with anti-HBs and anti-HBe negative. The serological diagnosis is:
ex: IgM anti-HBc indicates acute HBV infection; anti-HBs and anti-HBe appear later in convalescence.

q: A child with sickle cell disease has painful knee swelling; X-ray shows lytic lesions. Joint aspirate culture grows which organism most likely?
ex: Salmonella osteomyelitis is the classic complication of sickle cell disease, due to gut mucosal and splenic dysfunction.

q: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis is defined as resistance to which drugs?
ex: MDR-TB = resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, the two core first-line drugs.

q: A farmer has an ulcer with central black necrosis on his hand. Polychrome methylene blue staining shows capsulated bacilli with a positive M'Fadyean reaction. The diagnosis is:
ex: M'Fadyean reaction demonstrates the anthrax capsule on polychrome methylene blue stain; the black eschar (malignant pustule) is characteristic.

q: Group A Streptococcus attaches to fibronectin on pharyngeal epithelium primarily through which surface component?
ex: Lipoteichoic acid mediates GAS adherence to fibronectin-coated epithelial cells, the first step in pharyngitis.

q: A child has intense perianal itching at night; thread-like white worms are seen in the perianal region. The likely parasite is:
ex: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) lays eggs perianally at night causing pruritus ani; diagnosis is by the cellophane tape test.

q: A child has painful vesicles around the mouth. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear inclusions. The causative virus is:
ex: Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells supports HSV (or VZV); HSV-1 causes orolabial herpes in children.

q: A man with hemoptysis has BAL microscopy showing septate hyphae with acute-angle dichotomous branching. The fungus is:
ex: Aspergillus shows septate hyphae branching dichotomously at acute (45°) angles, unlike Mucor's broad aseptate right-angle hyphae.

q: A 30-year-old man with urethritis develops septic arthritis of the knee. Deficiency of which complement component predisposes to this disseminated infection?
ex: Deficiency of the membrane attack complex (C5-C9) predisposes to recurrent disseminated Neisseria infections.

q: Which vaccine strain is used to prevent congenital rubella syndrome as part of MMR?
o: Wistar RA 27/3 only for rubella is RA27/3
ex: RA 27/3 is the rubella vaccine strain used in MMR; Edmonston-Zagreb is measles, 17D is yellow fever.

q: A patient's screening ELISA for HIV is repeatedly reactive. The standard confirmatory test is:
o: Repeat ELISA with a different kit
ex: Western blot detects antibodies to specific HIV proteins (p24, gp41, gp120) and is the classic confirmatory test after screening ELISA.

q: A patient from Bihar has prolonged fever, splenomegaly and pancytopenia. Splenic aspirate shows intracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies. The confirmatory serological test of choice is:
ex: rK39 rapid test detects anti-Leishmania antibodies and is the point-of-care test for visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar).

q: A woman from West Rajasthan has an erythematous ulcer on her leg; edge biopsy shows organisms with dark nuclei and a kinetoplast. The likely agent is:
ex: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (oriental sore) is caused by Leishmania tropica; amastigotes show a rod-shaped kinetoplast beside the nucleus.

q: A fisherman has progressive swelling of his leg. Night blood smear shows sheathed microfilariae with no nuclei at the tail tip. The parasite is:
ex: W. bancrofti microfilariae are sheathed, show nocturnal periodicity and have an empty tail tip without nuclei.

q: A girl with lower abdominal pain has fever and a cervical lesion that bleeds easily. Wet mount shows motile flagellates. Which statement about the organism is correct?
o: It forms cysts in the female genital tract
It is transmitted by contaminated water
It shows jerky twitching motility on wet mount and is sexually transmitted
ex: Trichomonas vaginalis trophozoites show jerky motility on wet mount; no cyst stage exists and transmission is sexual.

q: Which biological indicator is used to monitor the efficacy of autoclave sterilization?
ex: Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores are the biological indicator for steam autoclaving; Bacillus atrophaeus is used for dry heat/ethylene oxide.

q: A woman developed fever, arthralgia and maculopapular rash after a trip; serology shows IgM to a virus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes that also causes congenital microcephaly. The virus is:
ex: Zika virus (Aedes-borne flavivirus) causes rash-arthralgia illness and congenital microcephaly in pregnancy.

q: A 40-year-old man has more than 5 hypopigmented hypoesthetic patches and a strongly positive slit-skin smear. What multidrug regimen and duration is correct by WHO criteria?
o: Rifampicin plus Clofazimine plus Dapsone for 12 months
ex: Multibacillary leprosy = 3-drug MDT (R+D+C) for 12 months; paucibacillary = 2 drugs for 6 months.

q: While on MDT for borderline leprosy, a patient's existing cutaneous lesions become acutely erythematous, swollen and tender within weeks. Which is the first-line treatment?
ex: Type 1 (reversal) lepra reaction is cell-mediated; treat with systemic corticosteroids.

q: A pregnant woman on 3-drug multidrug therapy for lepromatous leprosy develops painful erythematous nodules with fever (erythema nodosum leprosum). Which drug is absolutely avoided here because of teratogenicity?
ex: Thalidomide (DOC for ENL) is contraindicated in pregnancy; prednisolone/clofazimine used instead.

q: In a patient of leprosy, which single peripheral nerve is the most frequently affected, presenting as claw hand with ulnar distribution sensory loss?
ex: Ulnar nerve is most commonly involved; posterior tibial nerve is affected earliest.

q: A patient with heavy bacillary infiltration develops facial thickening with deep furrows and eyebrows fall, giving a lion-like appearance. Which form of Hansen disease is denoted by this sign?
ex: Leonine facies and madarosis indicate lepromatous leprosy.

q: A patient with a painless genital ulcer has a reactive VDRL. Which test most reliably confirms treponemal infection?
ex: Positive nontreponemal test (VDRL/RPR) needs modern treponemal confirmatory test (TPHA/FTA-ABS).

q: A child has notched, barrel/screwdriver-shaped permanent upper central incisors, interstitial keratitis early in life, and acquired nerve deafness. Which condition should be suspected?
ex: Hutchinson's trio: notched incisors + interstitial keratitis + 8th nerve deafness = late congenital syphilis.

q: An ulcerated, extremely painful, soft-edged ulcer with a yellowish base and painful inguinal adenopathy appears 4 days after unsafe sex. Which organism causes the condition?
ex: Chancroid = soft, painful ulcer by Haemophilus ducreyi; syphilis = painless indurated ulcer.

q: Multiple soft, cauliflower-like lesions of cauliflower na on perineum in a young man, long sina fingers absent, Biopsy-risk. Which HPV types are characteristically the low-risk strains in these warts?
ex: Condyloma acuminatum anogenital warts → low-risk HPV 6/11; types 16/18 are high risk.

q: A young woman with gluten-sensitive enteropathy has grouped intensely pruritic vesicles over fingers, elbows and buttocks; DIF shows granular IgA in dermal papillae. Which drug shows dramatic improvement?
ex: Dermatitis herpetiformis responds dramatically to dapsones; DIF = granular IgA at dermal papillae.

q: After repeated sun exposure at the face, a man with a mean superficial flaccid bullae leaving scale-crusts but no mucosal lesions. Anti-desmoglein profile showing which specificity helps a diagnosis of pemphigus?
ex: Pemphigus foliaceus biologically targets desmoglein 1 alone → superficial scaly skin No mucosal.

q: A woman with moderate to severe pemphigus vulgaris who is intolerant of long-course prednisolone. Which novel agent, added to corticosteroid, is a recognized first-line corticosteroid-sparing choice?
ex: Rituximab plus systemic corticosteroids is first-line for moderate-severe pemphigus vulgaris.

q: A 5-year-old has golden-yellow honey-coloured crusted erosions around the nose and mouth. Which organism is most commonly responsible?
ex: Non-bullous impetigo are honey-coloured crusts, Staphylococcus aureus most common.

q: A cluster of painful vesicular lesions along the mandibular? No — on the face along the side of the nose in an older man. The presence of a vesicle at the tip of the nose implies involvement of which nerve branch / (directishology)?
ex: Hutchinson's sign (nasal tip lesions) = nasociliary nerve involvement → risk of ocular zoster complications.

q: A febrile child had a developing, readily shiny, sharply demarcated, raised, warm plaque over the cheek. Which microbial agent is the classic cause?
ex: Erysipelas is sharply demarcated facial erythema, historically group A strept.

q: An obese diabetic male has a large tender, fluctuant tender swelling over the nape of the neck draining pus from multiple openings with deep abscess. Which organism most likely?
ex: Carbuncle = deep staph infection with multiple draining sinuses, neck of diabetics.

q: A 7-year-old has a scaly patch on the scalp with hair broken off near the follicles and black dot stubs; Wood's lamp shows bright green fluorescence. What diagnosis?
ex: Tinea capitis: broken hair with green Wood's fluorescence tends to Microsporum species.

q: A ring formation of red scaly plaque with central clearing has spread slowly on a villager's forearm. Which 1 is the classically described causative?
ex: Tinea corporis produces annular 'ringworm' plaques with clearing centre.

q: On Wood's lamp, golden-yellow ease; skin scrapings of the app of the trunk show short curved hyphae and spores looking like spaghetti with the meatballs. The DOC is?
ex: Pityriasis versicolor = Malform furfure (Malassezia); KOH 'spaghetti and meatballs'; topical azole DOC.

q: A farmer with painless swelling of the foot and multiple discharging sinuses has painless-buck granules in the discharge smear. Black firm granules composed of pigmented fungal hyphae indicate which class?
ex: Black grains = eumycetoma (true fungi); pale yellow grains = actinouretyma (bacterial).

q: A gardener with a nodule at the thumb after handling thorns develops nodular, (ascending) lymphatic proximal ulcerated. Which azole oral agent is the first choice?
ex: Sporotrichosis spread along lymphatics in a line; oral itraconazole is selected.

q: A 6-year-old child with atopy has ill-defined, dry, finely scaling hypopigmented patches only over the cheeks. Which benign hypopigmentary disorder is classic?
ex: Pityriasis alba: inconspicuous scaly hypopigmented patches on cheeks in children atopic.

q: Kligman's trio? Weather the triple combination cream used first-line in melasma comprises (select components)?
ex: Melasma Kligman cream = hydroquinone + tretinoin + mild topical steroid.

q: A woman with stable mucosal vitiligo enquires whether her other organs are at risk. Which associated condition is the most frequently seen concurrently?
ex: Vitiligo: most common autoimmune association is thyroid dysfunction.

q: A young woman with progressive pallor, fatigue, shows thin, brittle, concave spoon nails. Which state is responsible for koilonychia?
ex: Spooning (koilonychia) is classically linked to iron deficiency.

q: After a week of high fever, a patient later grows transverse furrows/depressions across all fingernails that appear as the fever resolves. What is the correct name?
ex: Beau's lines = transverse grooves from temporary interruption of nail matrix growth.

q: Twice within a few months after this same medicine, and this predicted dark purple sharply- limited patch arises at the identical site, leaving pigmentation. Which diagnosis?
ex: Fixed drug eruption recurs at same site after re-exposure; classic oral mucosal/gential lip site.

q: In a Chinese-origin adult, carbamazepine triggered Stevens-Johnson syndrome. The rapid screening test most relevant before prescribing the drug in individual
ex: Carbamazepine SJS associated with HLA-B*15:02; pre-screen in Han Chinese etc.

q: A 30-year-old with persistent itchy red swellings that come and go daily over more than 6 weeks and  u primary complaint. What is the first-line pharmacotherapy?
ex: Chronic spontaneous urticaria >6 weeks → non‑sedating antihistamine first‑line.

q: A young adult has recurrent painful, localized swelling attacks of the lips/larynx after throat and abdominal crises since childhood. Complement studies would disclose a deficiency of which protein?
ex: Hereditary angioedema = deficiency of C1-inhibitor; risk of laryngeal oedema.

q: A pigmented, velvety thickening in axilla and neck of a 45-year-old obese woman without response. It is most strongly predicting which internal condition?
ex: Acanthosis nigricans = papillo marker of insulin resistance.

q: In the brown papule with urticaria pigmentosa, gently rubbing the lesion causes it to become red and rise into an urticarial wheal. Name the sign.
ex: Darier's sign (wheezing urticaria on rubbing) typical skin mastocytosis.

q: In the groin fold and interdigital areas, a well-defined pink-brown patch shows coral-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Which group of organisms is responsible?
ex: Erythrasma (interdigital folds) fluoresces coral red due to Corynebacterium.

q: A machine worker has recalcitrant vesicular rash at the site of contact with a metal uniform, most likely allergic contact dermatitis. Patch test will most often pick up which metal?
ex: Nickel is the most common allergen; ACD is type IV hypersensitivity, diagnosed by patch test.

q: A 15-year-old girl with a family history of asthma and allergic rhinitis has itchy, flexural eczema. Thickened lichenified plaques over antecubital fossae since early childhood. Which condition?
ex: Atopic dermatitis: hereditary, age-flexor pattern, lichenification; juvenile form.

q: Which of the following tends to be a permanent, scarring alopecia (as opposed to reversible)?
ex: Lichen planopilaris destroys follicles → scarring alopecia; telogen uncommon.

q: Two months after recovery from a severe febrile illness with loss, diffusing, thinning of hair on the entire scalp at once in a woman; no scarring. Most likely diagnosis?
ex: Telogen effluvium: diffuse shedding pity 2–3 months after fever/stress; reversible.

q: An 18-year-old with severe nodulocystic nodulocyc acne with scarring in the face and shoulder is interested optimal drug choice. Which is the DOC?
ex: Nodulocystic acne → oral isotretin (teratogenic, needs contraception and lipids monitoring).

q: A nurse developed herpetic paronychia — a tender vesicular cluster on the finger pad after glove… which virus is responsible?
ex: Herpetic whitlow: primary HSV infection of the digit, at-risk healthcare workers.

q: An infant at 4 weeks has diffuse greasy yellow scaling over the scalp along with creases, folds and diaper friction. What diagnosis is consistent?
ex: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis presents as greasy 'cradle cap' scalp scaling.

q: In an adult, the dominant blood supply to the femoral head comes from which source?
o: Medial circumflex femoral artery via retinacular vessels
Artery of the ligamentum teres (foveolar artery)
ex: Retinacular (lateral epiphyseal) branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery supply most of the head; the foveolar artery is a minor contributor.

q: A 70-year-old woman slips and sustains an extracapsular intertrochanteric fracture of the femur. Which treatment is the standard choice?
ex: Intertrochanteric fractures have a rich blood supply and unite well; a sliding hip screw (DHS) is standard, and AVN is rare here.

q: Two days after a shaft of femur fracture, a man develops confusion, hypoxia with SpO2 unresponsive to high-flow oxygen, and petechiae over the chest, while the chest X-ray is clear. The diagnosis is:
ex: Fat embolism follows long-bone fractures by 24-72 h: hypoxemia, petechial rash, cerebral dysfunction, clear X-ray early.

q: After a road traffic accident, a patient's affected leg lies flexed, adducted and internally rotated with apparent shortening. Which injury fits this posture?
ex: Flexion-adduction-internal rotation is the classic posture of posterior hip dislocation, which risks sciatic nerve injury.

q: The most common type of shoulder dislocation is:
ex: Anterior dislocation predominates; the axillary nerve is most at risk, causing deltoid weakness and a patch of lateral-arm numbness.

q: A man sustains a mid-shaft humerus fracture and cannot extend his wrist or fingers afterwards. Which nerve is injured?
ex: The radial nerve winds through the spiral groove, so mid-shaft humerus fractures cause wrist drop; most palsies recover spontaneously.

q: Avulsion of the medial epicondyle of the humerus most commonly injures which nerve?
ex: The ulnar nerve runs behind the medial epicondyle; its injury gives clawing of the ring and little fingers and loss of finger abduction.

q: Which lesion pairs a fracture of the distal third of the radius with dislocation of the distal radioulnar joint?
ex: Galeazzi = distal radius fracture + DRUJ disruption ('the radius must be fixed'); Monteggia is its proximal-ulna mirror image.

q: A 5-year-old boy limps with pain in the hip and thigh, worse on activity. MRI shows avascular necrosis of the femoral head. The most likely diagnosis is:
ex: Perthes disease is AVN of the femoral head in children aged 4-8 years, predominantly boys, presenting with a painless-then-painful limp.

q: A 13-year-old obese boy complains of hip and knee pain with limited internal rotation of the hip. X-ray shows posterior and medial displacement of the femoral head relative to the neck. The management is:
ex: SCFE occurs in obese adolescents; the epiphysis slips on the metaphysis. In-situ pinning prevents further slip; the contralateral side is often prophylactically fixed.

q: A 5-year-old child has bilateral knee and leg pain with normal bone density. X-ray shows metaphyseal 'corner' (Frankel) signs and subperiosteal haemorrhage. The diagnosis is:
ex: Vitamin C deficiency disrupts collagen: corner signs, Wimberger ring and subperiosteal bleeds appear on X-ray while bone density stays normal.

q: A patient with an enlarged maxilla, progressive hearing loss and visual deterioration has a markedly raised serum alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium and phosphate. The diagnosis is:
ex: Paget's disease gives an isolated ALP rise with normal calcium/phosphate; skull involvement causes deafness and maxillary enlargement.

q: Which X-ray finding is the most specific pointer to osteomalacia in an adult?
ex: Looser (Milkman) zones are lucent cortical fissures typical of osteomalacia, which also shows low calcium/phosphate and high ALP.

q: A postmenopausal woman's DEXA scan shows a lumbar spine T-score of -3.2. How is this classified?
ex: DEXA T-score <= -2.5 defines osteoporosis; -1 to -2.5 is osteopenia. Central DXA of hip and spine is the reference standard.

q: A newborn with multiple long-bone fractures sustained in utero has blue sclerae and dental abnormalities. The likely condition and its basic defect are:
o: Osteogenesis imperfecta - defective type I collagen
ex: OI stems from type I collagen defects; blue sclera, dentinogenesis imperfecta and recurrent fractures, including prenatal ones, are hallmarks.

q: An adolescent has dull bone pain that characteristically wakes him at night and is dramatically relieved by aspirin. X-ray shows a small radiolucent nidus with surrounding sclerosis in the femoral diaphysis. The best definitive treatment is:
ex: Osteoid osteoma: night pain eased by NSAIDs, small nidus on CT; CT-guided radiofrequency ablation is the modern definitive treatment.

q: Which is the most common primary malignant bone tumour overall?
ex: Multiple myeloma (plasma cell neoplasm) is the commonest primary malignancy of bone; osteosarcoma is the commonest non-haematological one.

q: A 20-year-old woman has a gradually enlarging painless tibial swelling. X-ray shows an intramedullary lesion with a ground-glass matrix and thinning of cortex, and the femur shows a shepherd's-crook deformity. The diagnosis is:
ex: Fibrous dysplasia: ground-glass matrix, shepherd's-crook femur; McCune-Albright adds café-au-lait spots and precocious puberty.

q: A 5-year-old boy has a red, hot, swollen knee with high fever and refuses to bear weight. What is the single most important next step to confirm the diagnosis?
o: Aspirate the joint for analysis and culture
Order an X-ray and wait for the report
ex: Septic arthritis is an emergency; joint aspiration (WBC >50,000, Gram stain, culture) is diagnostic, followed by antibiotics and urgent drainage.

q: A 12-year-old boy has had a dull aching pain and mild swelling in the lower leg for six months, without fever. X-ray shows a well-defined round lytic lesion in the tibial metaphysis with a surrounding rim of sclerosis. The most likely diagnosis is:
ex: Brodie's abscess is subacute staphylococcal osteomyelitis: a small central lucency ringed by reactive sclerosis, typically in the tibial metaphysis.

q: Which angle is measured to quantify the severity of a scoliotic curve on a standing X-ray?
ex: Cobb's method uses the endplates of the most tilted end vertebrae; a curve of 10 degrees or more defines scoliosis.

q: A 26-year-old man has chronic low back pain with early-morning stiffness for over an hour, relieved by exercise, plus recurrent anterior uveitis. Which investigation is most useful for an early diagnosis?
ex: MRI detects acute sacroiliitis long before X-ray changes (bamboo spine); HLA-B27 supports but does not establish the diagnosis.

q: A patient has pain in the DIP and PIP joints and the first carpometacarpal joint, while the wrist and metacarpophalangeal joints are spared. The likely diagnosis is:
ex: Hand OA targets DIP (Heberden), PIP (Bouchard) and thumb CMC joints while sparing MCP joints and the wrist - the reverse of RA.

q: Pain felt only between 60 and 120 degrees of active shoulder abduction, with relief at the extremes, describes:
ex: Mid-range impingement of the rotator cuff and bursa under the acromion produces the painful arc between 60-120 degrees of abduction.

q: An obese man has burning pain and numbness over the outer side of the thigh, worse on standing and walking and relieved by sitting. Examination shows sensory loss only, with no weakness. The diagnosis is:
ex: Meralgia paresthetica is entrapment of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (L2-L3) at the inguinal ligament - purely sensory, relieved by hip flexion.

q: A rigid plate is used to compress and fix a fracture. By which mechanism does this fracture heal?
ex: Rigid compression plating produces primary bone healing - direct Haversian remodelling with no visible callus; casts and nails heal secondarily.

q: A patellar tendon-bearing (PTB) cast is most appropriate for which fracture?
ex: The PTB cast unloads the tibia through the patella, allowing early weight-bearing for tibial shaft fractures (especially distal two-thirds).

q: A 75-year-old man sustains a displaced intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck. What is the most commonly recommended management?
ex: Displaced intracapsular NOF in the elderly has high AVN/non-union rates, so arthroplasty (hemiarthroplasty) is preferred over fixation.

q: After trauma, a patient's leg lies flexed, abducted and externally rotated. Which injury is most likely?
ex: Anterior hip dislocation fixes the limb in flexion-abduction-external rotation; posterior dislocations do the opposite.

q: A 10-year-old boy with an extension-type supracondylar fracture cannot make an 'OK' sign (thumb-index ring) after the injury. Which nerve is involved?
ex: AIN is purely motor: weakness of flexor pollicis longus and index flexor digitorum profundus abolishes the OK sign, with no sensory loss.

q: A fracture of the neck of the fibula produces which of the following clinical patterns?
o: Foot drop with high-stepping gait and first-web-space numbness
Loss of sensation over the medial sole
Weakness of all calf muscles with absent ankle jerk
ex: The common peroneal nerve winds around the fibular neck; its injury gives foot drop (loss of dorsiflexion/eversion) and lateral-leg sensory loss.

q: Which combination of injuries constitutes the 'terrible triad' of the elbow?
o: Elbow dislocation + radial head fracture + coronoid process fracture
Elbow dislocation + medial epicondyle avulsion + ulnar nerve palsy
Radial head fracture + capitellum fracture + medial collateral tear
Olecranon fracture + radial head fracture + distal radioulnar injury
ex: The terrible triad - dislocation, radial head and coronoid fractures - is unstable and needs fixation of both fractures or radial head replacement.

q: A 5-month-old infant has a positive Galeazzi sign (apparent leg-length inequality) and an Ortolani clunk. What is the first-line treatment?
ex: DDH under 6 months is treated with a Pavlik harness (flexion-abduction); later diagnosis needs closed or open reduction with spica casting.

q: In the Ponseti method for clubfoot (CTEV), which deformity is corrected FIRST in the sequence of manipulations and casting?
ex: Ponseti order: cavus first, then adductus, varus and finally equinus (last by percutaneous Achilles tenotomy), followed by a foot-abduction brace.

q: A child walks with difficulty and has marked bowing of the legs. Serum alkaline phosphatase is 1322 IU/L with low phosphate. The most likely diagnosis is:
ex: Growing children with rickets show a striking ALP rise, low/normal calcium-phosphate, and cupped, frayed, widened metaphyses.

q: A 13-year-old boy has months of waxing-and-waning arm pain, low-grade fever and a raised ESR, with a destructive diaphyseal lesion on X-ray. Ewing's sarcoma and osteomyelitis both fit. What is the next best step?
o: MRI to differentiate and define tumour extent
ex: MRI precedes biopsy in suspected Ewing's - it distinguishes tumour from infection and maps soft-tissue extent for biopsy planning.

q: A 19-year-old man has knee pain and a lytic lesion in the epiphysis of the proximal tibia. Biopsy shows sheets of chondroblasts with a cobblestone pattern and chicken-wire calcification. The diagnosis is:
ex: Chondroblastoma arises in the epiphysis before physeal closure and shows 'chicken-wire' calcification; GCT is epiphyseal only after fusion.

q: The most common pattern of vertebral involvement in tuberculous spondylitis (Pott's spine) is:
ex: TB spreads along the anterior longitudinal ligament; the paradiscal pattern predominates, classically in the lower dorsal spine.

q: According to the WHO, which test is recommended as the diagnostic test for spinal tuberculosis?
ex: WHO recommends a nucleic-acid amplification test (GeneXpert MTB/RIF) on pus or aspirate for spinal TB; MRI remains the imaging of choice.

q: A 3-year-old child has fever of 39 deg C, refuses to bear weight, ESR 55 mm/h and WBC 15,000/cu mm. How many of the Kocher criteria are satisfied, and what is the likely diagnosis?
ex: Kocher predictors: fever >38.5 C, non-weight-bearing, ESR >=40, WBC >12,000; with all four the probability of septic arthritis is very high.

q: A 65-year-old woman gets leg pain radiating down both legs after walking about 100 metres, relieved by leaning forward, but climbs stairs without pain. Peripheral pulses are normal. The diagnosis is:
o: Lumbar canal stenosis with neurogenic claudication
ex: Neurogenic claudication is eased by lumbar flexion and unchanged by standing still; vascular claudication gives absent pulses and relief on standing.

q: A 35-year-old woman has symmetric pain and swelling of both wrists, MCP and PIP joints with morning stiffness lasting two hours, and the most specific serological marker would be:
ex: RA targets MCP/PIP and wrists symmetrically; anti-CCP is the most specific serological test and predicts erosive disease.

q: A patient with an open (Gustilo type III) fracture of the femur shaft arrives in the emergency room. Which step is NOT part of the immediate emergency management?
o: Immediate open reduction and internal fixation
ex: High-grade open fractures are stabilised with an external fixator after antibiotics and wound washout; internal fixation is delayed to avoid infection.

q: A 30-year-old woman has generalised bone pain and fatigue, X-ray shows diffuse osteopenia, and blood shows hypercalcaemia with hypophosphataemia. Which test would best localise the cause?
ex: Hypercalcaemia with hypophosphataemia and skeletal pain points to primary hyperparathyroidism; sestamibi localises the parathyroid adenoma.

q: A patient cannot initiate shoulder abduction; when the examiner releases the arm after lifting it, it falls, and passive elevation is full. Which tendon is most likely torn?
ex: A positive drop-arm test indicates supraspinatus (rotator cuff) tear; supraspinatus is the most commonly torn cuff tendon.

o: The inhibitor-enzyme complex has aged and cannot be reactivated
The antidote is destroyed by hepatic first-pass metabolism
Cholinesterases regenerate only after a week
The oxime dose fell below the therapeutic threshold
ex: Organophosphate poisoning: reactivation is possible only before the complex ages; pralidoxime plus atropine covers the acute window.

q: A child has eaten wild berries and presents with dilated pupils, flushed hot dry skin, dry mouth, tachycardia, absent bowel sounds, and hallucinations. Which class of poison best explains the picture?
ex: The anticholinergic toxidrome, hot as a hare, dry as a bone, red as a beet, mad as a hatter, is countered centrally with physostigmine.

q: In cardiogenic shock a patient receives dopamine at 6 mcg per kg per minute. Which receptor chiefly produces the inotropic effect at this rate?
ex: At 5-15 mcg/kg/min dopamine acts on beta-1; D1 at low dose and alpha-1 at high dose constitute the pressor ladder.

q: A patient on dabigatran needs emergency surgery. Which specific reversal agent is available for this anticoagulant?
ex: Dabigatran is reversed with idarucizumab, a humanized antibody fragment; protamine covers heparin, vitamin K covers warfarin.

q: The loop diuretic furosemide acts chiefly at which nephron site?
o: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
ex: Furosemide blocks Na-K-2Cl co-transport in the thick ascending limb, the highest-ceiling diuretic location.

q: A head injury patient with intact kidneys has rising intracranial pressure. Which diuretic is appropriate?
ex: Mannitol osmotically pulls water out of the brain; also used in dialysis disequilibrium and acute angle-closure glaucoma.

q: Soon after hemodialysis a uremic patient develops headache, confusion, and seizures. Which drug is used for this dialysis disequilibrium syndrome?
ex: Mannitol reduces the cerebral osmotic gradient during dialysis disequilibrium; slow the dialysis rate too.

q: A bipolar patient stabilized on lithium is prescribed a thiazide diuretic and within days develops coarse tremor, thirst, and confusion. Mechanism?
o: Thiazides decrease renal lithium clearance raising the serum level
Thiazides displace lithium from plasma proteins
Thiazides shift lithium into adipose tissue
ex: Thiazides raise serum lithium by reducing clearance; reduce the lithium dose and monitor levels when the pair is used.

q: Why is lamotrigine dosage escalated very slowly?
o: It causes severe bradycardia if loaded
It accumulates in fat with fast loading
Rapid titration risks serious skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome
ex: Fast lamotrigine titration or co-valproate raises the rash risk; slow upward titration protects, stop at first rash.

q: A woman with epilepsy is planning pregnancy. Which drug has the highest neural-tube-defect risk and is best switched before conception?
ex: Valproate carries the highest major-malformation burden (neural tube up to 2%); use the lowest effective dose or alternative.

q: Long-term use of which antiseizure drug characteristically causes gum hypertrophy?
ex: Phenytoin gingival overgrowth is dose-related; good oral hygiene protects, and the drug also gives hirsutism and folate fall.

q: Benzodiazepine overdose with respiratory depression - which specific competitive antidote is given intravenously?
ex: Flumazenil is the benzodiazepine antagonist; avoid it in mixed overdose because seizures can break through.

q: Methanol poisoning produces blindness and metabolic acidosis via accumulation of which toxic end-product?
ex: Methanol to formaldehyde to formate; fomepizole or ethanol blocks alcohol dehydrogenase and folate shunts formate.

q: A re-entry supraventricular tachycardia terminates within seconds of an intravenous bolus followed by flushing and chest pressure. Likely drug?
ex: Adenosine blocks the AV node with a sub-10-second half-life, hence its fleeting side effects; verapamil is the safer alternative.

q: Which antiarrhythmic carries a high risk of torsades de pointes because it blocks IKr and prolongs QT?
ex: Sotalol (class III) prolongs QT and risks torsades, particularly with hypokalemia; magnesium is the acute treatment.

q: Which lipid combination is notorious for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis and is best avoided?
o: A statin with a PCSK9 inhibitor
ex: Gemfibrozil interferes with statin elimination and boosts muscle toxicity; fenofibrate is the safer fibrate pair.

q: The PCSK9 inhibitors (e.g. evolocumab) lower LDL cholesterol mainly by what mechanism?
o: Preventing PCSK9-mediated degradation of LDL receptors, raising LDL clearance
ex: PCSK9 normally degrades LDL receptors; antibodies let receptors recycle, sharply lowering LDL as add-on therapy.

q: Which agent lowers cholesterol by inhibiting intestinal uptake via the NPC1L1 transporter?
ex: Ezetimibe blocks NPC1L1 at the enterocyte brush border; often combined with statins to reduce LDL further.

q: A diabetic patient with heart failure and chronic kidney disease needs an add-on with proven cardiovascular and renal protection. Best choice?
ex: SGLT2 inhibitors cut heart-failure hospitalizations and CKD progression; watch for euglycemic DKA and genital infections.

q: Which insulin analog gives a flat, peakless basal coverage lasting about 24 hours?
ex: Glargine is designed for a peakless basal profile; NPH has a distinct peak and shorter duration.

q: A patient on metronidazole for amoebiasis is told to avoid alcohol during and for 48 hours after the course. Why?
ex: Metronidazole inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, producing a disulfiram-like flush with alcohol; a classic drug interaction.

q: After a course of which antibiotic is toxigenic Clostridioides difficile pseudomembranous colitis most classically seen?
ex: Clindamycin is the classic trigger of C. difficile colitis; oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin is the treatment.

q: During a rapid intravenous vancomycin infusion a patient develops flushing, pruritus, and hypotension. Best explanation?
o: Red man syndrome from histamine release
ex: Rapid vancomycin infusions release histamine, causing red man syndrome; slow the infusion to over an hour.

q: A three-week-old infant has paroxysmal cough with apnea and lymphocytosis; pertussis is confirmed. The appropriate antimicrobial is?
ex: A macrolide such as azithromycin is the treatment of choice for pertussis in infants; clarithromycin is the alternative.

q: Which co-administered agent worsens the ototoxicity of an aminoglycoside such as gentamicin?
o: A loop diuretic such as furosemide
ex: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity is potentiated by loop diuretics; monitor renal function and drug levels.

q: Methotrexate inhibits DNA synthesis in cancer and rheumatoid arthritis mainly by blocking which step?
ex: Methotrexate blocks DHFR; leucovorin (folinic acid) rescue restores folate after high-dose therapy.

q: A first episode of genital herpes is best treated with which nucleoside antiviral?
ex: Acyclovir is the drug of choice for HSV infection; ganciclovir is preferred for CMV, oseltamivir for influenza.

q: Long-term hydroxychloroquine users need what ophthalmic surveillance because of a characteristic adverse effect?
o: Maculopathy (retinal toxicity) with early screening after 5 years or risk factors
ex: Hydroxychloroquine maculopathy is dose and duration dependent; baseline and then annual exams after about 5 years.

q: Before giving primaquine for radical cure of vivax malaria, which condition must be excluded to prevent hemolysis?
ex: Primaquine causes oxidative hemolysis in G6PD deficiency; screen first, and in G6PD deficiency consider weekly dosing.

q: In tumor lysis syndrome with rising uric acid, rasburicase lowers urate by which action?
o: Converting uric acid to soluble allantoin via urate oxidase
ex: Rasburicase is recombinant urate oxidase converting urate to allantoin; allopurinol prevents but does not degrade existing urate.

q: Which adverse effect of high-potency conventional antipsychotics like haloperidol is least responsive to anticholinergic treatment?
ex: Tardive dyskinesia is late, often irreversible, and does not respond to anticholinergics; acute EPS does.

q: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia responds best to which drug that nevertheless demands serial blood-count monitoring?
ex: Clozapine is unique for refractory schizophrenia but requires mandatory absolute neutrophil count surveillance for agranulocytosis.

q: A hypothyroid patient's TSH rises when omeprazole is added despite the same levothyroxine dose. The likely explanation is?
o: Drug interaction at the TSH receptor
Reduced levothyroxine absorption with higher gastric pH
ex: Gastric acid helps levothyroxine dissolution; acid suppression can lower absorption - take thyroxine on an empty stomach.

q: Which antiretroviral drug is the classic NRTI backbone for PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis)?
ex: TDF-FTC (or TAF-FTC) is the approved PrEP regimen; adherence is the key determinant of protection.

q: Maintenance therapy in opioid dependence with the longest-acting full agonist is?
ex: Methadone is a long-acting mu-agonist for maintenance; buprenorphine is partial agonist, naltrexone antagonist.

q: A bile acid sequestrant like cholestyramine works by?
o: Binding bile acids in the gut to promote their fecal loss, upregulating LDL receptors
ex: Resins bind bile acids and interrupt enterohepatic circulation; they also bind other drugs, so space dosing.

q: The most common cause of PPI failure to heal reflux esophagitis is?
o: Poor acid suppression from rapid CYP2C19 metabolism or non-compliance
ex: PPIs fail chiefly when acid suppression is inadequate; consider doubling dose or switching to a different PPI.

q: After starting inhaled corticosteroid therapy a patient develops oral thrush. Which measure prevents it?
o: Rinse the mouth after each inhalation and use a spacer
ex: Local oropharyngeal candidiasis from inhaled steroids is prevented by mouth rinsing and spacers; treat with nystatin.

q: During an acute gout flare, colchicine relieves pain chiefly by?
o: Inhibiting microtubule assembly and neutrophil chemotaxis
ex: Colchicine binds tubulin, dampening neutrophil migration and inflammation; it is not urate-lowering.

q: Which new diabetic drug class is associated with euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis in perioperative or dehydrated patients?
ex: SGLT2 inhibitors may cause ketosis without high glucose; hold the drug before surgery and sick days.

q: Severe salicylate intoxication with acidosis is treated with?
o: Sodium bicarbonate infusion and enhanced elimination
ex: Alkalinization traps salicylate in the urine; hemodialysis for severe poisoning; NAC is for paracetamol.

q: First-line drug in anaphylaxis is?
o: Intramuscular adrenaline in the anterolateral thigh
ex: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg is the anchor of anaphylaxis management; antihistamines and steroids are adjunctive.

q: A patient with angina develops tolerance to continuous nitroglycerin patch. The management strategy is?
o: Switch to sublingual only as needed
Provide a daily nitrate-free interval of 8-12 hours
ex: Nitrate tolerance follows continuous exposure; an 8-12 h nitrate-free interval restores efficacy.

q: Hypokalemia predisposes to digoxin toxicity because?
o: It increases digoxin binding to Na-K-ATPase
ex: Low potassium competes less at the pump, so digoxin toxicity emerges; maintain normokalemia in atrial fibrillation with digoxin.

q: Which tetracycline class effect restricts its use in children under eight years?
